title: What If You Flew a Spaceship Through the Asteroid Belt?

scenes.text: What if you flew through the asteroid belt? The movies lied.
Asteroids average nearly a million kilometres apart. That's about twenty-four times around the Earth.
There are more than a million asteroids wider than a kilometre, and the space between them is still enormous.
All of them together would make a world with only about three percent of the Moon's mass.
Pioneer 10 crossed in 1972. Voyager, Galileo, Cassini and New Horizons followed, all without incident.
One estimate puts the odds of hitting an asteroid in the belt at about one in a billion. It's not a minefield. It's almost nothing.

description:
What if you flew through the asteroid belt?
It is mostly empty space: asteroids sit nearly a million kilometres apart on average, and many spacecraft have crossed safely.
What should we run through next?
